one_liner: A U.S. Public Health Service officer (O-5) who runs healthcare risk management, incident reviews and patient-safety audits for ICE detention health services.
fit_summary: Open only to commissioned U.S. Public Health Service officers and call-to-active-duty candidates with a healthcare credential and an advanced degree. Daniel has public health emergency experience but no commission or healthcare license, so he can't be selected.
eligibility: Restricted: open only to USPHS Commissioned Corps officers and Call to Active Duty (CAD) candidates, not the general public, despite the 'public' hiring-path tag.
Must be a Registered Nurse, Nurse Practitioner/Physician Assistant, or in a Healthcare or Healthcare Administration related field, with a qualifying degree for the officer category.

Advanced degree (e.g., MPH, MA, MS) plus at least four years of relevant professional experience, including two years in public health program management, quality improvement, or risk management/compliance.
Certification in Healthcare Quality or Risk Management (CPHQ strongly recommended), or the ability to obtain it within one year.
Must maintain USPHS basic readiness, meet the physical demands (CPR, lifting, austere environments), and travel up to 30%.
keywords: data analysis for tracking, trending, and reporting
program development, review, implementation and evaluation
strategy: Skip it: it needs a USPHS commission and a healthcare credential.
Redirect his effort to roles that fit what he has now, such as FEMA or DHS emergency management specialist, program analyst, or preparedness positions open to the public.
Look at Virginia VDEM and Prince William County or Manassas emergency management jobs, and at legislative staff roles that use his policy knowledge.
interview_questions: Describe how you conducted or supported a root cause analysis and turned the findings into a corrective action plan.
How would you monitor compliance with PBNDS, NCCHC, and ACA standards across facilities, including those not staffed by IHSC?
Tell us about a time you used data trends to drive a policy or practice change.
How do you handle sensitive inquiries raised by outside groups, such as NGOs, about detention conditions?
watch_outs: Status-only posting: USPHS officers and CAD candidates only. Daniel, as a civilian with no commission, is ineligible.

Requires a clinical or healthcare degree and an advanced degree, plus a healthcare quality or risk management certification or the ability to earn one within a year; his M.A. is in Global Affairs, not a healthcare field.
The work involves heavy physical demands, austere detention settings, up to 30% travel, and possible 30-day TDYs.
The salary listing ($1–$150,000) is a placeholder; actual pay follows USPHS O-5 rank pay.
